## Description

TinyLlama ctxpp4/genpp4 can exhaust its 300-second readiness deadline while Blackwell workers are still initializing and warming up. Increase only this test's startup deadline to **900 seconds** and remove its B200/B300 waives for NVBug 6771023. The latest B300 cold-cache diagnostic reached cluster readiness in **639.988 seconds**, so neither the initially proposed 500 seconds nor 600 seconds covers that run. A 900-second budget provides about 260 seconds of headroom; this is not a worst-case bound.

Integrate and extend the diagnostics from [PR #19304](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19304): phase/shape timings, percentages, slow-phase warnings, PID/rank identifiers, and profiling/final-executor warmup purpose and pass numbers. Add startup timing around MPI and worker readiness, model/executor initialization, resource allocation/teardown, existing rank barriers, HTTP startup, service registration and complete cluster readiness. Nested phases are excluded from outer totals; parent-process waits overlap worker execution and must not be summed across processes. Failed phases retain elapsed time and propagate exceptions.

These are host-side measurements using existing synchronization; no CUDA synchronization, barriers or collectives are added. Attention timing includes model forward, first-touch JIT and waiting rather than pure compiler time. Logs follow existing filtering; Python API users can enable them with `TLLM_LOG_LEVEL=INFO`. Worker-exit detection remains active.

This PR adjusts the timeout and adds diagnostics. It does not optimize startup; investigation of model initialization, compilation/cache reuse and autotuning will be a separate follow-up.

## Test Coverage

Target integration test: `disaggregated/test_disaggregated.py::test_disaggregated_ctxpp4_genpp4[TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0]` (8 GPUs).

| Platform / run | Tested readiness budget | Cluster launch-to-ready | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B300 / isolated JIT caches | 900 s | **639.988 s** | **1 passed**, full pytest **672.58 s** |
| B200 / isolated JIT caches | 500 s | **228.326 s** | PASS |
| B200 / cache reuse | 500 s | **93.144 s** | PASS |

B300 was tested on `dc36700308` with a per-invocation 900-second override. Commit `5fcc8be33c` makes that same timeout the test's source default; this final timeout/comment-only revision has not been separately GPU-rerun. B200 was tested on `9311771ce1`.

B300 cold-start breakdown (two rank-0 workers running concurrently):

| Stage | Measured wall time |
| --- | --- |
| Model initialization | approximately 294 s |
| Sampling module warmup | 84.5–84.6 s |
| Attention warmup | 149.7–149.9 s |
| Autotuner | 22.7–23.5 s |
| First warmup total, including the warmup stages above | 265.5–271.0 s |
| Second internal warmup pass | 0.8–1.2 s |

The second internal pass is part of the same startup, not a separate hot-start run. The startup/warmup log validator passed after correcting its expected PID count to cover both passes on all eight ranks; pytest passed independently, while the original wrapper exit code reflected that validator issue. A successful current-implementation B300 hot-start measurement is still outstanding: the preceding cache-reuse attempt failed on a 60-second NCCL initialization timeout.

**CPU regression tests:** 13 added cases; **32 passed, 22 deselected** (GPU cases excluded), covering:

- `_StartupTimer`: nested/repeated phase accounting, unattributed time, failed-phase timing, exception propagation and depth restoration.
- Warmup diagnostics: repeated phases, exception timing, empty/zero-duration summaries and slow-warning threshold boundaries.
- Executor creation: profiling and final allocation phase names/order, including both estimation and direct-allocation paths.

`unittest/test_startup.py` is explicitly listed in `l0_cpu.yml`; the other two test files are covered by the existing `unittest/_torch/executor` directory entry, with the new cases marked CPU-only. Pre-commit and the targeted readiness-argument check passed for the final change.

Cold runs isolate FlashInfer, Triton, Torch-extension and CUDA caches; OS page caches are not globally cleared, and weights remain on shared storage. These are individual measurements rather than a worst-case startup bound. The 900-second budget leaves approximately 260 seconds of headroom relative to the measured B300 readiness time.

### zhaoyangwang-nvidia · 2026-09-22

@lori-ren, replying to the three points in your [review](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/19402#pullrequestreview-5268229347):

1. **Logging controls:** These logs only run during startup and warmup, using host-side timers without adding CUDA synchronization or collectives. We expect negligible startup overhead and no steady-state inference impact. They fill a gap in basic startup diagnostics, so we'd prefer to keep them enabled by default and use the existing log-level controls rather than add a separate switch.

2. **Timer class:** Done. Moved the timing state, phase/shape logging, summaries, and slow-phase warnings into a reusable `_WarmupTimer`. `ModelEngine` now holds a single timer instance. Updated the regression tests; all 41 CPU tests pass.

3. **Startup optimization:** We plan to optimize startup time in a follow-up. These logs are the first step toward identifying where the time goes. This PR focuses on fixing the readiness timeout and adding the missing diagnostics; it does not include startup optimizations.

### lori-ren · 2026-09-21 · CHANGES_REQUESTED

Leaving three questions, code changes may be required:
1. Should we make the startup timer optional? Seems that the timer is enabled by default and user can't disable it even if they are not interested in profiling.
2. This PR adds `_warmup_*` fields and related methods directly to ModelEngine, which is too intrusive. I think it's better to provide a universal class which provides internal states for timers and methods for recording. ModelEngine only holds an instance instead of all its states and methods.
3. Follow-up: 900s timeout is very long and could result in low GPU utilization and long CI time. Mark a follow-up task to accelerate startup and warmup for PP.
